en: For you to sit there gaping
Is disgraceful;
Stand by your word
And wage your greatest battle.
The khan who vowed to grapple is dead;
All who clashed with them are dead.
The earth was shattered and shaken;
Seven thousand torments and a thousand deaths
Descended upon our heads at once.
A cannon shot came for nothing,
A troop of life-destroyers came;
The lion Choro and hero Seytek—
A shock like these two came,
A deep-dug chasm came,
And misery came upon every living soul.
A messenger has come—give your answer;
Understand what I have told you.
Oh Sarybai, heed my words!
Having attacked a lion blessed by Kyzır,
Let us not camp along the ravine;
Though guiltless and without blame,
Let us not be slaughtered for nothing!
Let us not lose our homeland
And flee away in panic;
Let us not lose our consummate army
And run away in flight!
Take my words as counsel;
Come, Sarybai, heed my words!
Driven by rage and boasting of valor,
We attacked the lion blessed by Kyzır;
Acting with savage intent,
Today we are caught in death’s snare.
No man has ever come forth
To face that ill-starred bloodthirsty tyrant;
No enemy has faced and defeated him.
No one has ever drawn close,
No neighboring foe has conquered him.
With an army covering the earth,
We unleashed a raid and loosed the host,
Raining arrows down like rain.
For every hero we tethered
Four steeds for him to ride.
Mounting the red-roan horse,
He broke the hard ground and opened a path;
Külchoro and Seytek, the two giants,
Came straight at us and attacked.
Seers died and khans died;
Everyone who witnessed them died.
The stars scattered from the heavens
As Külchoro and Seytek joined forces.
Though I pleaded, they would not hear my words;
They tormented me,
Stripped my robe away as spoil,
And wantonly dug my grave,
Bringing marvels down upon my head.
We have fallen into the fierce one’s grasp;
Our strength is gone though we remain alive,
Black blood pours from our lungs;
Only by dying did we escape.
You are the strength on which I relied,
My renowned one, my lion;
Thus have we fallen into torment—
How can we escape death?
The hour of our death has come.”
After he had spoken thus,
Like one pierced in a vital gland,
Like a prince stricken with fever,
Like a man whose wife is crushed by nightmare,
He paled, as though his roots were dead,
As though his whole world had been scattered;
His bellowing split the stones,
His shouting split heads,
His eyes flared like fire;
The hair of his body stood on end,
And he roared loudly.
Like a rutting camel in winter,
His wild temper raging,
He crackled and thundered;
Every mortal human being’s
Whole body shuddered.
Growling and working himself into fury,
He poured out his wrath, thundering
At the messenger who had brought the news:
“Who would listen to these words of yours?
Let the dog that came to the ship hear them;
Let the fluttering bird hear them;
Let the hard earth below hear them;
Let the unbroken sky above hear them;
Let the surging river water hear them;
Let the pitch-black night hear them;
Let the demon from Mount Qaf hear them—
Who else but these would listen?
Is Zhelpinish some cheap and worthless land?
Is Sarybai some feeble hero?
The wretched descendant of Manas
Is far beneath me in valor.
This is the path by which I surveyed
The rugged hills and hollows of Talas;
This is the arm that speared
That vagabond Choro six times!”
He thundered, working himself into fury;
The crackling madman
Spoke like lightning:
“If what you have said is true,
Then, bereft of my vast army,
I have indeed been a brutish fool;
My horn has broken from my head,
And I have been left hornless.
Taking my pit for level ground,
Taking my wretched self for a hero,
I have come to utter ruin.
When I consider the calamity I have met,
I see that I am finished.”
Saying this, Sarybai
Recoiled from his true army;
He saddled his horse Tookyzyl,
Put on his bulletproof armor,
And his savage fury showed.
When Sarybai strode forth in rage,
Those crowned and seated on thrones
Despaired of their royal lives;
Those who grazed the black earth and saw the sun
Despaired of livestock and life;
Worms, insects, and every creature
Despaired of their lives.
He fully unleashed his venom,
And it engulfed the whole world.
Hearing it clearly, Sarybai
Poured out his wrath like this;
He doubled so many over
That the black earth could not stir,
And the great multitude halted.
When the warrior stood roaring,
When he shouted his command,
Heads spun in bewilderment,
And the world filled with dust.
When he raged and lunged,
He began a mighty upheaval;
Under the force of his fury, many men
Were left without a single hair,
And began to perish.
Startled by the words he had heard,
He saddled the peerless steed Tookyzyl,
Saddling Tookyzyl for battle;
He seized his cannon and roared,
Summoning those skilled at mounting horses,
The strong men resourceful in danger,
The tents that sheltered them from the cold,
Every hero’s stratagem,
And warriors who came without being summoned—
United in soul, sharing death together.
If he dies, we share one blood,
While alive, we are fellow countrymen,
While safe, we are companions,
Sharing one name, we are comrades,
Sharing our gains, we are neighbors,
While safe, we gather together,
While alive, we are companions,
We have slept in one bed,
We have shared the same delights,
We have hunted game together,
We grew up from childhood,
We lived badly, then prospered,
We lived poor, then grew rich,
We went without, then gained abundance,
Our camps stood side by side,
Our valleys were shared,
If safe, we shall gather together,
If alive, we shall be companions,
Come share counsel, come, my lion,
Every grief and grievous pain—
Come, my hero, resolve it now,
This is my word—behold:
For God's sake and for mine,
I shall gladly meet them in combat,
Though the people wail and heroes die,
Though all are utterly spent,
Stand behind me as my support,
I shall attack Külchoro,
I shall unleash my wrath on Seytek,
I shall bring slaughter upon the Kyrgyz,
I shall summon strength into my arms,
If she falls into my hands, I shall humiliate her,
I shall violate Chürök,
Brave men, old and young,
Say, “Sarybay has given the command,”
Do not grieve; satisfy your desire,
Let one of the seven days bring death,
Why should I live on in vain?
Let me gladly meet them, thrusting spears,
Let us grapple violently,
Let me perish fighting to the end,
Aichürök is the one I desire,
Kuyaly, on whom my enemies have set their sights,
That radiant beauty—
I shall ride straight at her and seize her,
If turmoil and strife erupt on every side,
Drawing bows like pouring rain,
Shooting arrows like hail,
When the lion's eyes blaze,
When his blood-drinking frenzy seizes him,
I shall settle the score in full,
Making the Kyrgyz shriek,
I shall drive them away and plunder them,
If Külchoro struts,
I shall beat the old madness from him,
If the Kyrgyz roar,
I shall divert the water from their riverbed,
If they boast of their young hero,
I shall snuff him out like a fire,
Thus spoke Sarybay,
Making the wide world narrow as a grain,
Such was his furious state,
Unable to withstand his wrath,
The whole vast army marched out,
From the dreadful rage of that swine,
His very flesh bristled,
His eyes sank deep as pits,
When that swine flew into a frenzy,
Unable to withstand his wrath,
Of the scouts standing watch,
Several were slaughtered,
Whatever he faced became flame,
Whatever he attacked ceased to exist,
Nothing remained for him to behold,
Those he routed came to a halt,
Such was Sarybay's state,
Rushing about in frantic haste,
When grief made his eyes blaze,
Whenever the wretch grew angry,
The vast army roared and misery seethed,
Despairing of their fly-like lives,
He saddled Tookyzyld,
His spirit estranged and divided,
When he glowered in fury,
He looked ready to suck them dry,
Such was Sarybay's state:
Sixty wrestlers and forty warriors
Fell one by one in their places,
Upon Tookyzyld,
Into the steel-soled stirrups,
He leapt without even setting foot,
Alone from the massed army,
He rode visibly forth to single combat,
He appeared ready to drain
Every mortal human being,
A savage frenzy seized him,
Against that dread man's wrath,
No one could stand,
His appearance utterly transformed,
Chasing the whole wide world,
Drawing breath like a dragon,
He looked ready to suck all life away,
His eyes distorted and blazed,
Tookyzyld's reins
He gripped now right, now left,
